title: Score the riddle
description: Turn the player's replies into numbers, and keep score when a riddle is solved or missed.

tasks.title: Replies are always text
tasks.body: input() always gives back text, even when the player types digits. So "5" + "5" joins into "55" instead of adding up to 10. int(...) turns text like "12" into the whole number 12, and float(...) turns "2.5" into the decimal 2.5.
tasks.detail: Wrap the reply in int(), like points = int(input("Points? ")). If the reply is not a whole number, such as ten or an empty reply, int() stops with a ValueError. When a reply might be empty, compare it with "" before you convert it, as the example on the next card does.

tasks.code:
# Ask for the gold in your pocket, as a whole number
gold = int(input("Gold in your pocket? "))
# Ask for the bridge toll; an empty reply means no toll
toll = input("Toll? ")
if toll == "":
    toll = "0"
# Turn the toll into a number, then pay it
print(gold - int(toll))
tasks.note: With 20 and 5 as replies, it prints 15. An empty toll becomes the text "0" first, so int() has a digit to read. Without int(), Python could not take text away from a number.

tasks.question: If the player types ten in letters for the gold, what happens?
tasks.why: int() only understands digits, like "10". The letters ten are not a whole number, so Python stops with a ValueError on line 2. You can try it on the next card.

tasks.prompt: Run the example with 20 and 5. Then predict, and run, each of these: an empty toll, and the letters ten as the gold. Last, delete int( and its ) from the gold line, run it, and read the explanation. Reset code puts the example back.

The riddle keeper says how many points a riddle is worth. Ask for the hero's score, then for the riddle's points, and turn both replies into whole numbers yourself. Print two lines: the score if the riddle is solved (the points are added), then the score if it is missed (the points are taken away). An empty points reply means a practice riddle worth 0. Print just the two numbers.
tasks.starter:
# Ask for the score and turn the reply into a whole number
# Ask for the riddle's points; an empty reply means 0
# Print the score if solved, then the score if missed
hints: Three steps: get the score as a number, get the points as a number (or 0 when the reply is empty), then print the two results.
Look at the second comment. Keep the points reply as text until you have checked whether it is "", and only then turn it into a number.
A pattern with other names: reply = input("Coins? "), then if reply == "": with an indented line that gives reply the text "0", then coins = int(reply).

error_hints.text: One test leaves the points reply empty, and int() can't turn empty text into a number. Check whether the reply is "" before you call int().
input() gives text. Text can't be taken away from a number, and + joins text instead of adding. Wrap each reply in int(...) before you calculate.
Give each name a value before you use it, spelled the same each time. Each input() reply needs a name of its own.
This challenge gives your program two replies: the score, then the points. Use exactly two input() calls.
With a score of 10 and a riddle worth 3, the first line is 13 (solved) and the second is 7 (missed). Check the order of your two print() lines.
Missing a riddle can take the score below zero: 5 - 8 is -3. Print the result as it is; a negative score is fine here.
With an empty points reply, the riddle is worth 0, so both lines show the score unchanged.
Calculate from the replies, not from numbers typed into the code, so your program works for every score.
Every reply counts, even a score of zero. Calculate from the replies rather than checking for particular numbers.

similar_example.code:
reply = input("Lanterns? ")
if reply == "":
    reply = "1"
lanterns = int(reply)
print(lanterns * 2)
similar_example.note: An empty reply becomes the text "1" before int() reads it, so the program never stops. Your challenge uses 0 for an empty reply, and needs two numbers.

other_ways.code:
score = int(input("Score? "))
points = input("Points? ")
if points == "":
    points = 0
else:
    points = int(points)
print(score + points)
print(score - points)
other_ways.note: if and else can each give points its number.

other_ways.code:
score = int(input("Score? "))
points = int(input("Points? ") or "0")
print(score + points)
print(score - points)
other_ways.note: or picks "0" when the reply is empty. A later lesson explains or properly.

input_labels: Toll (a number, or leave it empty)

cases.description: a score of 10 and a riddle worth 3
a score of 5 and a riddle worth 8
a score of 6 and an empty points reply
starting from a score of zero
